title: Craig interpolation for Gödel logic with function symbols
formal: In first-order Gödel logic over [0,1], without built-in equality and allowing function symbols, does every pair of sentences phi,psi with \(\varphi\models_1\psi\) admit a sentence theta in their common nonlogical vocabulary such that \(\varphi\models_1\theta\) and \(\theta\models_1\psi\)?
definitions:
A structure has a nonempty domain. Function symbols of every finite arity, including constants, are interpreted as ordinary total functions; an r-ary predicate is interpreted as a map from domain^r into [0,1]. Terms receive domain values in the usual way. Truth values of conjunction and disjunction are min and max. The implication a⇒b has value 1 when a≤b and value b otherwise. Bottom has value 0, top 1, and negation is abbreviation for implication to bottom. Universal and existential quantifiers are infimum and supremum over all domain elements.

The relation phi models_1 psi means every structure over the union of their vocabularies that gives phi value 1 also gives psi value 1. The interpolant may use only predicate, function and constant symbols occurring in both sentences, with their original arities. It may introduce bound variables but no new nonlogical symbols. There is no equality symbol, similarity predicate, truth-value constant other than 0 and 1, or Delta connective. The target is sentence interpolation for this explicit truth-preserving consequence relation; no complexity or size bound on theta is required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked interpolation theorem for arbitrary finite sentence vocabularies with functions, or an entailing sentence pair together with a proof that no sentence in its common vocabulary interpolates. A theorem restricted to relation and constant symbols does not settle the function-symbol case.
context: Khatami, Pourmahdian and Tavana prove interpolation for relational vocabularies with constants. Their conclusion explicitly leaves languages with function symbols as a further question.
why: The question asks whether common vocabulary still suffices to explain entailment once functions enter a many-valued logic.

import_provenance.original_title: Craig interpolation for Gödel logic with function symbols
import_provenance.original_statement: Does first-order Gödel logic with truth values [0,1], allowing function symbols and without built-in equality, have Craig interpolation? Whenever A entails B, the desired interpolant I must use only their common nonlogical symbols and satisfy A entails I and I entails B.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The relational-language case, with constants but no function symbols, was settled positively before the cutoff; the cited paper explicitly leaves this extension open.
